# Claude chat fixtures

`claude-2.1.302-local.jsonl` and `claude-2.1.302-question-local.jsonl` were recorded on 2026-10-16 from installed Claude Code 2.1.302 in print/stream-JSON mode. Each run used a disposable repository and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, a fake local-only API key and an HTTP server on loopback that supplied synthetic Messages responses. No provider request or paid usage occurred. This tests the actual CLI envelope and tool/question round trip, not authenticated model behavior.

Common arguments were checked with `claude --help`: `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions --append-system-prompt <fixture instructions> --session-id <uuid>`. The question run added `--permission-prompts host --permission-prompt-tool stdio` and a correlated initialization control request. The help's permission-prompts description names the latter flag; its stdio value and response envelope were corroborated against Anthropic's Python SDK subprocess/control reference and then exercised against the installed binary. The application implements the records in Rust and embeds no SDK.

Metadata, paths and random ids were removed or normalized; message ids and distinct block-record UUID identities remain represented. Notably, separate text and tool records share the same assistant message id. The question fixture preserves a correlated `can_use_tool` request and the tool-result envelope after an explicit synthetic answer.

`claude-2.1.302-background-local.jsonl` was recorded on 2026-10-17 from the same installed Claude Code 2.1.302 with the same arguments and setup (disposable repository, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `HOME`, fake local-only key, loopback synthetic server, no provider request). One user record was written; the synthetic first response ran Bash with `run_in_background: true` (`sleep 2`), and the turn settled. When the command finished, the CLI started its own turn with no stdin input: `system/task_updated`, `system/task_notification` and `system/background_tasks_changed`, then `system/init`, narration, a foreground tool, the final text and `result`. Startup and `--resume` printed no `system/init` before input in separate runs. Paths, task ids and record UUIDs were normalized; only fields Shika reads or that identify the record kind were kept.

`claude-chat.jsonl` is hand-written from the documented format to exercise thinking, subagent text, partials, duplicate records and an aggregate result containing intermediate text. Negative/multiple-text-block/error cases are also constructed directly in Rust tests. Tests never spawn a real Claude process or read normal provider files.

Primary references: [programmatic guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless), [user input](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/user-input), [subprocess flags](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/transport/subprocess_cli.py), [control protocol](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/src/claude_agent_sdk/_internal/query.py).

## Codex

The `codex-0.162.1-*-local.jsonl` files were recorded on 2026-11-20 from installed codex-cli 0.162.1 running `codex app-server` (stdio, the default `--listen stdio://`; flags checked with `codex app-server --help`). Every run used a disposable git repository with a detached linked worktree at `.worktrees/shika-lead` as the cwd, an empty disposable `CODEX_HOME` and `HOME`, a minimal `PATH`, a fake local-only key, and a Python HTTP server on loopback that returned scripted Responses API SSE streams. No provider request, real account, or paid usage occurred. The provider was set per process: `-c model_provider="synth"`, `-c model="gpt-5"`, `-c model_providers.synth.{name,base_url,env_key,wire_api="responses",request_max_retries=0,stream_max_retries=0}`, plus today's trust override `-c projects={"<worktree>"={trust_level="trusted"}}`. The driver wrote `initialize` (`clientInfo {name: "shika"}`), `initialized`, `thread/start {cwd, developerInstructions, approvalPolicy: "never", sandbox: "danger-full-access"}`, then `turn/start {threadId, input: [{type: "text"}]}` per turn, and closed stdin to stop.

Format: one JSON object per line, `{"dir": "send" | "recv", "msg": <JSON-RPC frame>}` in wire order, with `{"dir": "spawn", "msg": {"args", "cwd"}}` before each process and `{"dir": "exit", "msg": {"code"}}` after its stdin was closed. Records are otherwise unmodified: unknown notifications (`remoteControl/status/changed`, `warning`, `thread/status/changed`, `thread/tokenUsage/updated`, `account/rateLimits/updated`, deltas) are kept so decoders are tested ignoring them. Sanitized: paths became `/fixture/repo`, `/fixture/repo/.worktrees/shika-lead`, `/fixture/codex-home` and `/fixture/home`; the loopback port became `<port>`; the host name became `fixture-host`; every UUID (thread, turn, item, installation, rollout file name) was replaced consistently within a file by `00000000-0000-7000-8000-<n>`. `00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000000` is the deliberate missing id. Message ids (`msg_*`) and call ids (`call_*`) are the synthetic server's own.

- `normal`: two turns. Turn 1 has commentary, two `exec_command` tools, a `partial_answer`, then a `final_answer` (the server set the Responses `phase` field and Codex passed it through). Turn 2 repeats with no `phase` at all.
- `question`: launched with `--enable default_mode_request_user_input` (an under-development feature). Without it, the default mode returns "request_user_input is unavailable in Default mode" to the model and no server request is sent. Shows `item/tool/requestUserInput` (`isBlocking: false` in default mode), the answer `{"answers": {"<question id>": {"answers": ["<label>"]}}}`, and `serverRequest/resolved`.
- `interrupt`: `turn/interrupt {threadId, turnId}` while `sleep 37` ran; the response is `{}` and `turn/completed` arrives at once with `status: interrupted`, then a further turn continues the thread. The tool process kept running after the interrupt (see the plan's Codex evidence note).
- `failure`: one session with `stream_max_retries=2`: an HTTP 500 (retried twice, then failed), a `response.failed` stream (retried twice, then failed), a stream that failed twice then succeeded, and a normal turn. Retries are `error` notifications with `willRetry: true`; only `willRetry: false` and `turn/completed` `status: failed` end a turn.
- `background`: a turn Codex starts itself. The model called `create_goal`; after the turn completed, Codex opened a goal continuation turn (`turn/started` with no `turn/start` from the client and no `userMessage` item), and the model completed the goal with `update_goal`.
- `subagent`: `spawn_agent` (namespace `multi_agent_v1`). The child thread's `thread/status/changed`, `turn/started`, items and `turn/completed` arrive on the same connection with the child's `threadId`; the parent started no turn of its own when the child finished.
- `resume`: process 1 starts a thread with instructions A and runs one turn; process 2 runs `thread/resume` with instructions B and `excludeTurns: true`, one turn, then `thread/resume` of the missing id (`-32600 "no rollout found for thread id ..."`) and of a non-UUID (`-32600 "invalid session id: ..."`).
- `resume-tui`: `thread/resume` of a thread created by the interactive TUI (`codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox ... "<prompt>"` in a PTY, same disposable home and server), then one turn. The resumed thread reports `source: "cli"`, `originator: "codex-tui"`. This file was recorded before the driver wrote `spawn`/`exit` lines, so it has none.

`codex-0.162.1-app-server-schema.json` is a subset of `codex app-server generate-json-schema --out <dir>` from the same binary (non-experimental): the method lists and only the records and fields Shika sends or reads. The full bundle is about 4.4 MB; regenerate it rather than committing it.

## Pi

The `pi-1.4.0-*-local.jsonl` files were recorded on 2026-11-20 from installed Pi 1.4.0 in RPC mode. Each run used a disposable repository, a disposable `HOME` and `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, `PI_OFFLINE=1`, `PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1` and `PI_TELEMETRY=0`. The agent directory held a `models.json` with one custom provider (`api: "openai-completions"`, `baseUrl` on loopback, a fake local-only key) and a `settings.json` that shortened retry backoff (`retry.baseDelayMs: 200`, `retry.maxRetries: 2`) and set `compaction.keepRecentTokens: 10` so compaction had something to summarize. A Python HTTP server on loopback answered every chat-completions request from a fixed script. No provider request or paid usage occurred, so these test Pi's own RPC envelope, run lifecycle, retry and compaction, not authenticated model behavior.

Arguments, checked with `pi --help`: `--mode rpc --approve --model synthetic/synthetic-model --session-id <uuid> --append-system-prompt <fixture instructions>`. The question, interrupt and background runs added `-e <fixture extension>`, a disposable extension that registers an `ask_question` tool (`ctx.ui.select`), a `confirm_question` tool (`ctx.ui.confirm`), a `/fixture-handled` command and a `/fixture-later` command that calls `pi.sendUserMessage` after 1.5 seconds. Stock Pi 1.4.0 ships no question tool and starts no turn by itself; these records show what Shika must handle when a user's or Shika's own extension does.

Each line is one stdout record, in order, except lines of the form `{"fixture_stdin": {...}}`, which are the exact commands the recording client wrote to stdin at that point. Sanitizing replaced paths with `/fixture/...`, timestamps with fixed values, extension UI request UUIDs with `fixture-ui-N` and session entry ids with `fixture-entry-N`; the system message's built-in prompt sections are replaced with placeholders (the `addendum` section, which carries `--append-system-prompt`, is kept), and `toolsAdded` keeps only tool names. Session ids were chosen synthetic UUIDs and are unchanged. Everything else is verbatim, including `message_update` deltas and `agent_end.messages`.

- `normal`: `get_state`, then two prompts: narration plus a tool, narration plus a second tool, and a final; then a tool call with no text and a final. The first run of each process starts with a `role: "system"` message pair.
- `question`: a `select` answered with a value, a `select` answered `cancelled: true`, and a `confirm` answered `confirmed: true`.
- `interrupt`: `abort` during a `sleep 30` bash tool; a further prompt in the same process; `abort` while an extension `select` is pending, which does not settle until the client answers the dialog (here `cancelled` after 3 seconds); `abort` while the provider is still responding; a last prompt.
- `failure`: a non-retryable 400 (no retry), then a 503 that exhausts two retries. Both settle with `aborted: false`; the failure is only in the last assistant `stopReason: "error"` and `errorMessage`.
- `recovery`: a reply whose reported usage crosses the threshold, followed by `compaction_start`/`compaction_end` between `agent_end` and `agent_settled`; then a stream cut mid-text (assistant `stopReason: "error"` carrying the partial text) that is retried and succeeds inside one settled run.
- `overflow`: a tool turn whose next request fails with "prompt is too long": `agent_end` has `willRetry: false`, then overflow compaction with `willRetry: true`, a new `agent_start`, the final, and one `agent_settled`.
- `background`: `/fixture-handled` (`disposition: "handled"`, a `notify` request before the response, no run), an unknown `/not-a-command` (sent to the model as text), a prompt while busy without `streamingBehavior` (`success: false`), a `followUp` prompt (`disposition: "queued"`, `queue_update`, delivered inside the same run with no `agent_end` between), and `/fixture-later`, whose turn starts with `agent_start` and no pending prompt.
- `resume`: a new process with the `normal` session's `--session-id` and changed instructions; `get_state` reports the same id and `messageCount: 11`, and the system message carries only the new addendum.
- `resume-missing`: `--session-id` with an id that does not exist; `get_state` reports that id with `messageCount: 0` (stderr only: "No project session found with id ...; creating a new session with that id.").

Primary references: the installed package's `docs/rpc.md`, `docs/rpc-commands.md`, `docs/rpc-extension-ui.md`, `docs/json.md`, `docs/models.md`, `docs/settings.md` and `docs/environment-variables.md`.

## Cursor CLI

The `cursor-2026.11.19-*-local.jsonl` files were recorded on 2026-11-20 from installed Cursor CLI 2026.11.19-f005e9d in ACP mode (`agent ... acp`, protocol version 1). Cursor has no local provider route, so every run used the author's real Cursor login (Decision 6 in the plan) and made real, small requests with the account's default model. Each run used a disposable git repository and a disposable `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` whose `cli-config.json` set `approvalMode: "allowlist"` with an empty allowlist, so the permission records show what the flags do rather than a user setting. The login itself came from the keychain; the author's global Cursor config was not edited. A small Python client wrote the requests and recorded both directions; nothing was approved on the author's behalf (the probe client rejected every permission request).

Flags were checked with `agent --help` and `agent acp --help` (no options of its own). Unless a file says otherwise, the launch was `agent --force --trust --sandbox disabled acp`. Every `initialize` sent `clientCapabilities { fs: { readTextFile: false, writeTextFile: false }, terminal: false }`, and every session used `mcpServers: []` except `tools` and `permission`, which added one disposable stdio MCP server (`probe`, one `probe_echo` tool).

Each line is `{"from": "shika" | "agent", "frame": {...}}` (one JSON-RPC frame as written to or read from the pipe, in order) or `{"from": "process", "event": "exit", ...}` for how the child ended after stdin was closed. Sanitizing replaced paths with `/fixture/...` and `/home/fixture`, the user name with `fixture`, every UUID with `00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000N` (consistent within a file, so the session id and tool call ids still correlate; the newline inside `toolCallId` is kept), random tool call suffixes with `composer_call_fixtureN`, the model list with one `fixture-model`, `available_commands_update` with only the built-in `copy-request-id` (the real list carried the author's own commands and skills), `updatedAt` with a fixed value, and one em dash in model text with a plain dash. Everything else is verbatim, including thought chunks.

- `normal`: `initialize`, `session/new`, two turns: chunks, two tools (`ls -la`, read), more chunks and a final; then one tool and a final. `.cursor/rules/shika-lead.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`, "end every reply with RULE-A-PINEAPPLE") existed only while `session/new` ran; both finals end with that token. Clean exit after stdin close.
- `tools`: shell, an edit (with a `diff` content block) and an MCP call (`MCP: tool`, then `probe: probe_echo`) with no permission request under `--force`. Stdin close did not exit while the MCP server lived (SIGTERM after 10 seconds, exit 143).
- `permission`: the same prompt with `agent --yolo --trust --sandbox disabled acp`. `--yolo` is ignored in ACP mode: `session/request_permission` for the shell command and the MCP tool, both answered `reject-once` by the client; the edit needed none.
- `interrupt`: `session/cancel` one second into `sleep 20`; `stopReason: cancelled`, then a further turn in the same process.
- `background`: a shell command started in the background; the turn ends with `end_turn` and nothing more arrives in 40 seconds of idle (no CLI-started turn). Stdin close did not exit (SIGTERM after 20 seconds, exit 143).
- `resume`: a new process loads the `normal` session with rule B ("RULE-B-MANGO") present during `session/load` only; the replay arrives before the load response, and the reply still ends with rule A's token. Then a second process: `session/load` of a terminal-era chat id (from `agent create-chat` plus one `agent -p --resume` turn) and of a missing id, both -32602 `Session "<id>" not found`, then `session/list`.
- `failure`: launched with `-e http://127.0.0.1:9` (an unreachable endpoint): `initialize` succeeds, `session/new` fails with -32603 "Failed to initialize session services", and `session/prompt` on an unknown session fails with -32603 and `data.details`. No provider error inside a turn could be provoked with a real account.

Not recorded: `cursor/ask_question`. The model reported no AskQuestion tool in agent or plan mode, with the default model or composer-2.5. Its request and result shapes are described in the plan's Cursor findings, read from the installed bundle.

Primary references: `agent --help`, `agent acp --help`, the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com) schema, and the installed bundle's ACP modules (`src/acp/`) for behavior the recordings could not reach.
